September 9, 2026 – TheNewswire - Vancouver, British Columbia - Andina Copper Corporation (TSX-V: ANDC | FSE: FIR | OTCQB: PMMCF) (“Andina” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce the appointment of Shae Frosst as Vice President, Investor Relations. The Company also announces the grant of incentive stock options and Restricted Share Units (“RSUs”).
Joseph van den Elsen, Andina Copper President and CEO commented:

“I am very pleased to introduce Shae Frosst as our VP, Investor Relations, and to welcome her to our growing management team. This new role will allow us to expand our investor engagement strategy in support of Andina’s rapidly evolving story, and the numerous corporate and project level catalysts on the horizon.”

Ms. Frosst is an Investor Relations and corporate communications professional with over 12 years of experience in the mining sector. Shae brings extensive experience developing strategic IR plans, managing investor communications, and supporting M&A transactions for publicly traded exploration and production companies. Before joining Andina Copper, Shae held senior Investor Relations roles at New Found Gold Corporation, Centerra Gold Corporation, and Denison Mines Corporation.
Grant of Incentive Stock Options & Restricted Share Units (“RSUs”)

The Company has granted a total of 3,000,000 stock options of a 5-year term to the Company’s President & CEO. 1,000,000 are exercisable at $1.50, 1,000,000 are exercisable at $2.00, and 1,000,000 are exercisable at $2.50.
The Company has also granted a total 28,870 RSUs to certain employees, to vest twelve (12) months following the date of grant.

ABOUT ANDINA COPPER
Andina Copper Corporation is a unique South America-focused copper explorer listed on the TSX Venture Exchange

, Frankfurt (FSE: FIR), and OTC (OTCQB: PMMCF) exchanges. The Company holds two significant discoveries along the world’s premier copper producing Andean porphyry belt in Argentina and Colombia, and a compelling undrilled copper-gold target in the prolific copper production district of the Coastal Cordillera of Chile.
